jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Beth Jacob Congregation of Irvine (Beth Jacob) is an over 40\-year\-old modern\-orthodox congregation located in beautiful Irvine, California. We pride ourselves on our highly diverse community, which permeates our environment, and fosters an atmosphere of community, cooperation and mutual respect among Jewish traditions from around the world. We are also the only Shul in Orange County that has services up to three times a day, 365 days a year.

Beth Jacob is in search of our next Executive Director. The Executive Director of Beth Jacob Congregation of Irvine is a professional, full\-time staff member responsible for the day\-to\-day operation of the Synagogue, as well as a critical component of the short\- and long\-term strategic planning and growth of the Synagogue. The Executive Director works in collaboration with the Rabbi, President, Board of Directors, BJI Staff and others to identify the Synagogue’s priorities and align the Synagogue’s limited resources in a way that maximizes benefit to the community and creates sustainable growth.

The Executive Director must have world\-class organization and interpersonal skills with the ability to handle multiple priorities concurrently. The Executive Director must exhibit maturity and sensitivity toward the community with a strong sense of trust and confidentiality.

Representative duties that may be executed, delegated, or supervised include the following:

**A. Administrative:**

* Oversee all aspects of day\-to\-day Synagogue administration in coordination and alignment with the Rabbi, the President and BJI Staff.
* Effectively lead, manage and evaluate the Synagogue staff.
* Collaborate with the Director of Olam Jewish Montessori, as well as interface with the board of the Irvine Community Mikveh.
* Create office procedures and maintains a cooperative, pleasant working environment.
* Oversee the creation of the synagogue’s annual budget, and the implementation and performance in accordance with the budget.
* Build and strengthen the synagogue’s volunteer base.
* Implement policies of the synagogue as approved by the Board.
* Attend all general board meetings, as well as committee meetings as needed/requested.

**B. Membership and Fund Raising:**

* Work with representatives of the board to create, lead and implement short\-term and long\-term fundraising strategies.
* Coordinate and administer the Synagogue’s membership drives, aimed at member retention and growth in new membership.
* Welcome new and prospective members and attempts to integrate them into the synagogue family.
* Plan and coordinate events, as well as help establish groups, to attract and retain members representing different demographics (e.g., young couples, singles, seniors, women, etc.).
* Ensure the continued and growing success of annual fundraisers, including Purim baskets, annual calendar, yizkor book and more.

**C. Programming and Events:**

* Organize the synagogue’s master calendar and make it available to the community.
* Work with the Rabbi to maintain and grow adult education programming.
* Work to ensure the success of the BJI Annual Gala and other annual events, including Purim.
* Bring new programs and ideas to the shul.

**D.** **Youth Programming**

* Identify and implement new programs to attract and retain youth at the Synagogue, including Shabbat and High Holiday programming for multiple age groups.
* Work with the Rabbi to maintain and grow existing youth programming, including Youth Enrichment Classes and NCSY.

**E.**  **Strategic Planning and Community Outreach:**

* In coordination with the President and Board of Directors, create annual goals for the synagogue that cascade to staff members.
* Work with the Rabbi, President and board representatives reach out to members and potential members of the synagogue to strengthen relationships and assess needs and desires.
* Work with the Rabbi, President and board representatives to devise, implement and measure/monitor the synagogue’s 3\-5 year strategic plan.
* Establish and maintain accurate membership data, as well as effective methods of communication and publicity.
* Attend synagogue activities and events.
* Connect with the Orthodox Union and peers at other synagogues to bring best practices to the Synagogue and to leverage resources.

**F. Facilities Management**

* Responsible for long term and short term maintenance of all synagogue facilities, including janitorial staff and contractors for repairs and grounds maintenance, in coordination with staff and volunteers.
* In coordination with the Rabbi, develop and oversee the successful operation of the Synagogue’s kitchen facility.
* Work closely with members, accommodating their needs for their lifecycle events (e.g., schedules, set\-up of facilities, building usage fees, catering and any other arrangements).
* Oversee the development, implementation and maintenance of a disaster plan.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or demonstrated experience in nonprofit management, business administration, Jewish communal service, or related field preferred.
* Minimum of 5 years of leadership or management experience in nonprofit, educational, religious or community organizations
* Demonstrated experience in operational management of $500k\+ organizations. Hands on experience with budgeting, financial management, and organizational operations.
* Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal skills, supervisory and team leadership skills, and problem solving skills.
* Experience working with boards, volunteers, and diverse stakeholders

**Requirements**

* Strategic thinker with strong operational skills
* Collaborative and relationship\-oriented leader
* High level of integrity, discretion and professionalism
* Ability to balance multiple priorities and manage change effectively
* Commitment to fostering an inclusive environment for all individuals and families

Founded in 2018, Squash on Track is a non\-profit after\-school enrichment program guided by the mission to improve the lives of youth in Redwood City. Students in the program learn how to play squash, receive academic and other support tailored to their needs, and become part of a supportive community centered at Squash Zone, a state\-of\-the\-art squash center with nine squash courts and dedicated academic space. With an operating budget of $350,000, Squash on Track enrolls approximately 20 elementary and middle school students and aims to expand to at least 40 students by 2028\.

* ● Manage and run the daily **youth program** in a manner which ensures exceptionalprogramming, maximum enrollment, and excellent attendance, in\-year and longitudinalretention.
* ● Lead a comprehensive **development/fundraising** effort to build the financial assets of theorganization by raising an annual surplus and undertaking capital and endowmentcampaigns as required.
* ● Lead and develop SoT **personnel** to ensure the attraction, development, and retention oftop talent and longevity of leadership within the organization.
* ● Oversee, manage, and maintain the organization’s **physical assets and facility needs**.
* ● Oversee all matters of **fiscal and legal compliance** for the organization, ensuringcomprehensive “good standing.”
* ● Develop the **Board of Directors** and work closely with them to build the organization.
* ● **Evaluate** the program’s **impact** on its students and other constituents, and share thedetails of such impact with the Board of Directors annually.
* ● Work with the SoT community to develop a **strategic plan**, and subsequently executetoward plan goals.

Qualifications \& Core Competencies

* ● **Education \& Leadership:** Bachelor’s degree is a baseline, however, exceptionalprofessional achievement or other qualifications will be considered (graduate degree a plus). Proven success managing, developing, and inspiring a professional nonprofit or sports\-based youth development team.
* ● **Mission Alignment:** Understanding of and commitment to the “squash and education” model. Extensive experience working with under\-resourced youth, building parental relationships, and operating effectively across lines of cultural and socioeconomic difference.

**Job Description**  

New York City Emergency Management (NYCEM) helps New Yorkers before, during, and after emergencies through preparedness, education, and response. NYCEM is responsible for coordinating citywide emergency planning and response for all types and scales of emergencies. We are staffed by more than 200 dedicated professionals with diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise, including individuals assigned from other City agencies.  

  

The Office of the Chief Counsel provides legal advice to NYCEM executives and staff regarding critical, strategic, legal and policy issues facing the agency, engages in transactional work in support of the NYCEM mission and coordinates with the NYC Law Department, Office of the Chief Counsel to the Mayor and City Hall, and other local, state and federal counsels regarding various legal issues ranging from emergency events to litigation, which impact the agency. The Office of Chief Counsel is comprised of the Legal Affairs Unit, the Civil and Human Rights Unit formerly known as the Disability, Access and Functional Needs Unit (DAFN), and the Records Management Unit.  

  

The Records Management Unit is responsible for leading and managing the NYCEM records management program. It develops and implements policies and procedures to manage agency records throughout their life cycle, from creation to their final disposition, and works with units and personnel to ensure all staff are aware of and can apply records management best practices into their daily course of business.  

  

The Office of the Chief Counsel is seeking a Deputy Director of Records who will oversee work of the Records Management unit and supervise the Records Program Manager and any temporary staff, including interns. The Deputy Director of Records will oversee the maintenance and management the agency’s electronic and physical records. This includes any day\-to\-day responsibilities and creating and implementing policies around agency records. The Deputy Director of Records will work with staff to ensure that all records are in compliance according to City policies and procedures.  

  

Under the supervision of the Chief Counsel, the Deputy Director of Records will have responsibilities including but not limited to the following:  

  

* Overseeing Records Management unit staff and interns.
* Managing and maintaining an electronic records management system, currently RecordPoint’s Records365\.
* Performing day\-to\-day records management tasks and activities relating to storage, retrieval, retention and disposition of records.
* Training staff in the procedures related to policies governing the maintenance of all documents (both records and non\-records, regardless of format) and ensuring staff are aware of their role in the management of agency records.
* Overseeing all Records Management unit functions and projects including but not limited to reviewing and updating the retention schedule as needed, applying retention to records in SharePoint using Records365, creating destruction and transfer requests, choosing a system to manage physical records (potentially Records365\).
* Developing and implementing agency records management policies and related procedures as needed and performing yearly reviews and updates of established policies.
* Creating one page infographics to communicate important policies or procedures to NYCEM staff as needed.
* Overseeing all scanning projects which must follow the NYC Department of Records and Information Services’ (DORIS) processes and guidelines and be approved by DORIS before projects may commence. * Maintaining filing system procedures and classification indexes.
* Assigning and managing file space as well as inventorying boxes and preparing materials for storage or transfer to the NYC Municipal Records Center if needed.
* Working with staff to ensure all agency publications that are required to be submitted to the NYC Municipal Library are transferred to the Records Management unit for submission to the Library’s Government Publications Portal.
* Choosing, inventorying and cataloging materials in the agency library and managing patrons and the circulation of the collection utilizing ResourceMate Plus.
* Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex assignments, exercise sound judgment, and communicate progress to leadership.

EOC teams are on call for three weeks at a time, with six weeks off in between.

**About Back to the Bible**

Back to the Bible is an 87\-year\-old ministry that exists to help everyone, everywhere know, love, and be transformed by God's Word. Founded in 1939, the organization served as a radio ministry through 2020 before entering a new chapter built around digital biblical content and Bible engagement research.

The ministry does two things well: producing daily biblical content and conducting transformative research at the Center for Scripture Absorption. Since 2025 it has experienced renewed momentum, growing its YouTube audience to more than 130,000 subscribers, and the CSA undertaking research projects on a global scale. The organization is moving quickly and changing fast.

**About the Role**

Back to the Bible is looking for an experienced fundraising leader to build the strategy, systems, and rhythm behind a development operation entering a season of renewed momentum. Over the past year the ministry has stabilized and rebuilt its operations \& focused heavily on renewing \& expanding its donor base. The Director of Development will take that foundation and operationalize it.

The ministry carries a rich legacy and a large existing donor base. Roughly one third of revenue comes from planned and estate gifts, one third from major donors, and one third from general donors. Appeals and newsletters already generate a strong response and have real room to perform better. Digital fundraising is largely untapped beyond a monthly email appeal and a digital newsletter, even as the ministry's digital audience grows rapidly.

This role is split roughly in half. One half is designing and running the annual giving program: appeals, newsletters, monthly donor acquisition, digital fundraising, donor journey and appreciation, and reactivation of lapsing donors. The other half is direct donor work: carrying a portfolio, upgrading donors with the capacity to give more, and meeting with supporters in person where it is strategic.

The Executive Director remains highly active in fundraising, particularly in new major donor cultivation. The Director of Development will work alongside a major gifts officer and a donor relations coordinator and will partner closely with the Directional Leadership Team on organizational fundraising priorities.

*The central priority is converting a fast\-growing audience into donors and strengthening the donors the ministry already has, so that revenue relies less on unpredictable estate gifts.*

* Design and run the annual giving calendar, including print appeals, newsletters, and email campaigns
* Build the ministry's digital fundraising program and convert viewers, listeners, and readers into donors
* Develop and execute a monthly donor acquisition strategy alongside the development team w/ the goal of growing recurring revenue
* Create a donor journey and appreciation strategy that measurably improves retention
* Identify lapsing donors and design reactivation campaigns

**Donor Portfolio and Major Gifts**

* Carry and manage a portfolio of donors, with a particular focus on upgrading donors who have the capacity to give more
* Identify and qualify new prospects using wealth screening and data analysis
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward gifts, tailoring outreach to each donor's connection to the mission
* Visit donors in person where appropriate and strategic
* Partner with the Executive Director and major gifts officer on cultivation and solicitation strategy

* Collaborate with the content and marketing teams to produce fundraising materials, collateral, and donor communications

* Represent Back to the Bible at conferences and community functions
* Conduct meetings and presentations with donors and prospective ministry partners
